meta.description: Free citizen tool to check audiovisual content suspected of AI manipulation. Delivers verifiable signals, not verdicts.
intro.title: Check an image, a video or a URL
intro.text: FREETRUE-IA analyzes the content in your browser and returns verifiable signals anyone can reproduce — not a verdict. Nothing you upload leaves your device.
dropzone.text:
Drop an image or video here,
or click to select
dropzone.note: Max 100 MB · Processed in your browser
url.hint: Note: due to browser security (CORS), many sites won't allow direct download of their media. If it fails, download the file manually and upload it via the File tab. Reverse-search links work regardless.
results.title: Analysis report
card.reverse.text: Upload the image (or a video frame) to these search engines to check whether it has appeared before in another context. You do this step — it's the strongest evidence you can obtain.
card.news.text: If the content presents a news claim, check whether it appears in mutually independent outlets and whether any fact-checker has addressed it. A big story that only shows up in one place is the simplest and strongest red flag.
card.news.note: You don't need to know JSON or Git — the form prepares a pre-filled issue; you just review and press «Submit» on GitHub.
claim.label: Claim to check (edit or type):
claim.placeholder: e.g. «Government X announced today the removal of all Y support»
checklist.text: Review these signals with the image/video in front of you:
community.text: Like other platforms' community notes — but transparent and ownerless. Your input is filed as a public GitHub issue; anyone can discuss it, and if it adds real value it gets integrated following the process in docs/comunidad.md.
community.description: Short description of the content (1 line)
community.description.placeholder: e.g. Video attributed to X announcing Y
community.aportacion.placeholder: Explain clearly what you're adding and why it matters.
community.author: Your name or handle (optional)
community.conflicts.placeholder: none / I work at X / relative of Y
disclaimer: ⚠️ This report is not a verdict. Missing metadata or missing C2PA credentials do not prove manipulation. A high score from an automatic detector can be a false positive. The tool helps you look better; the final judgment is yours. When in doubt, don't share.
pillars.title: How it works
pillars.1.title: 1. Runs in your browser
pillars.1.text: Files never leave your device. No server, no cookies, no tracking.
pillars.2.title: 2. Reproducible signals
pillars.2.text: You can verify every data point on your own. We're not asking you to trust us.
pillars.3.title: 3. Public case database
pillars.3.text: Every analyzed case is recorded in an open, versioned repo with immutable history.
pillars.4.title: 4. Radical independence
pillars.4.text: No parties, no agendas, no compromising sponsorships. And if we ever disappoint you, fork the project.
footer.text: FREETRUE-IA · Code MIT · Cases CC BY 4.0 ·
footer.disclaimer: Citizen non-profit project. Does not replace professional fact-checking journalism — it confirms and validates without bias through the community and your personal check.
panel.title: Dashboard and search
panel.subtitle: All cases published in the FREETRUE-IA public database, filterable and visualizable.
verdict.title: Verdict traffic light
verdict.prompt: After reviewing all signals, your personal assessment:
verdict.modified.label: Which part is modified? (required)
verdict.modified.placeholder: e.g. The overlay text «...» was not said by the person in the original video; compare with the source on TVE, minute 03:12.
verdict.note: Your verdict is recorded in the downloadable report. The automatic signal (colored, above) comes only from technical evidence — it never replaces your judgment.
verdict.reason.default: Automatic signal: default yellow until a human validates. Review the signals below and mark your verdict.
verdict.reason.db_authentic: Automatic signal: matches a case already analyzed as authentic in the public database.
verdict.reason.db_manipulated: Automatic signal: matches a case already analyzed as manipulated in the public database.
verdict.reason.db_inconclusive: Automatic signal: matches a case already analyzed as inconclusive.
verdict.reason.c2pa_detected: Automatic signal: C2PA marks detected — review what they declare before concluding.
verdict.reason.human: Human verdict: assigned after reviewing the signals.
verdict.modified.required: You marked «False or modified»: describe which part is modified before downloading the report.
share.banner: You are viewing a shared report. Data comes from the link; the public-database comparison has been recomputed live.
wayback.title: 🗄️ Wayback Machine (web archive)
ela.note: Recompresses the image and amplifies the differences: edited or pasted areas often «glow» differently. Most reliable on JPEG. A uniform map does not prove authenticity and high-contrast edges glow naturally — it is one more signal, not a verdict.
frames.note: Extract key frames to analyze them as images: reverse-search each one, run OCR on frames with text, or download them as evidence.
hash.phash: Perceptual hash: identifies the image even if it was recompressed or resized. Distances ≤ 10/64 bits mean «same image to the eye».
quiz.title: Quiz — Can you spot it?
quiz.subtitle: Test your method against disinformation. No signup, no stored score — just learning.
quiz.final.good: Excellent critical eye. Share it: teaching the method multiplies its effect.
quiz.final.mid: Good instincts — review the «How to look» guide to round out your method.
quiz.final.low: Good news: the method takes 10 minutes to learn. Read the «How to look» guide and retry the quiz.
